title: Quant Market Brief — October 25, 2026: Gradient Integrity & PMI Pressure

stories.headline: New softmax paper identifies two numerical gradient failures
stories.fact: A new preprint describes Softmax Collapse, where a dominant target logit can produce a zero target gradient, and Softmax Cancellation, where equal student and teacher logits can produce nonzero gradients. The authors propose corrected implementations and report improvements in their experiments.
stories.inference: Numerical integrity can be a hidden source of training instability.
stories.uncertainty: These are author-reported findings; they do not establish that a particular MATLAB release or your model has either defect.
stories.why: Test extreme logits, gradient-sum consistency and equal teacher/student cases before changing an implementation.
stories.short: A softmax preprint identifies collapse and cancellation errors in numerical gradients. Add targeted gradient checks; do not assume a specific MATLAB implementation is affected.
stories.alt: Two conceptual panels show a dominant-logit gradient collapsing and equal student/teacher logits producing a nonzero gradient, followed by an implementation-audit box; no numerical magnitudes are asserted.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Barron et al., arXiv:2610.31642v1, October 22, 2026. Conceptual numerical-audit diagram.

stories.headline: Concentrated-liquidity model improves forecasts only in compatible regimes
stories.fact: A preprint models concentrated-liquidity profiles with a stochastic partial integro-differential equation. Calibration on three Uniswap pools improved active-band forecasting versus a martingale benchmark on two pools compatible with the stationary specification; the third showed out-of-sample nonstationarity.
stories.inference: Liquidity level, slope and curvature may be useful states, provided regime compatibility is checked.
stories.uncertainty: This AMM study does not validate a U.S. equity order-book model or establish profitable trading.
stories.why: Compare structural forecasts with a simple benchmark and quarantine a model when stationarity diagnostics fail.
stories.short: A concentrated-liquidity preprint beats its benchmark on two compatible pools but flags nonstationarity in a third. Model validity should be regime-conditional.
stories.alt: A conceptual flow diagram shows a liquidity-profile model tested against a martingale benchmark, with two compatible pools and one nonstationary pool; no forecast-error values are invented.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Lee et al., arXiv:2610.30539v1, October 21, 2026. Conceptual validation map; no calibrated equity-book curve.

stories.headline: Investors’ preference shifts toward quality over momentum
stories.date: MarketWatch analysis updated October 24, 2026, 9:37 a.m. ET
stories.fact: MarketWatch reports a recent investor preference for quality shares over previously strong momentum stocks.
stories.inference: Portfolio demand can change before a factor’s longer-term performance ranking reverses.
stories.uncertainty: The accessible report does not establish current SPY/QQQ depth or synchronized flows for our proxy ETFs.
stories.why: Separate flow narratives from measured returns and execution conditions.
stories.short: A new MarketWatch analysis reports preference for quality over momentum. Treat this as positioning context, not evidence of current ETF depth or a guaranteed reversal.
stories.alt: A qualitative positioning diagram shows reported investor preference toward quality and away from momentum, with a warning that fund flows, factor returns and executable depth are separate measures.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; MarketWatch analysis, updated October 24, 2026. Qualitative positioning schematic; no flow amounts asserted.

stories.headline: Flash PMI remains strong as selling-price pressures intensify
stories.date: S&P Global October flash release and analysis, October 23, 2026
stories.fact: S&P Global’s flash U.S. Composite Output PMI eased to 57.6 from September’s 58.4, remaining above the 50 expansion threshold. Its analysis also reported intensifying supply constraints and the sharpest selling-price increase in more than four years.
stories.inference: Growth resilience and inflation pressure can coexist, complicating a simple easing narrative.
stories.uncertainty: Flash survey estimates are revisable and are not realized GDP or CPI.
stories.why: Retain output and price components separately and use release-time vintages in macro-conditioned models.
stories.short: Flash Composite PMI eased to 57.6 from 58.4 but remained expansionary; S&P Global flags stronger selling-price pressure. Survey signals are not realized GDP or inflation.
stories.alt: Two zero-based bars show September Composite PMI of 58.4 and October flash PMI of 57.6, with a clearly labeled expansion threshold at 50.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; S&P Global, October 23, 2026. Composite Output PMI index points; October is a flash estimate.

stories.headline: Jio’s IPO attracts more than $77 billion in bids
stories.fact: Reuters reported more than $77 billion in bids for Jio Platforms’ IPO and public subscriptions exceeding 22 times the shares offered.
stories.inference: Demand for a large digital platform can remain strong despite pressure elsewhere in technology.
stories.uncertainty: Bids are not proceeds or guaranteed aftermarket returns.
stories.why: Separate subscription demand, allocation, valuation and post-listing liquidity.
stories.short: Jio’s IPO drew over $77bn of bids and public subscriptions above 22 times the offer. Bids are not proceeds, allocations or guaranteed listing gains.
stories.alt: Separate cards show more than 77 billion dollars in reported bids and public subscriptions over 22 times the shares offered; a note explicitly says neither equals IPO proceeds.
stories.credit: Market State Lab; Reuters, October 23, 2026. Bid demand and subscription multiple are separate measures.
